topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces complement as the lecture's subject and frames its importance and complexity.

topics.label: Overview of complement activation and functions
topics.groupedBecause: This overview establishes how complement activation connects pathogen recognition to immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions and exceptions needed to follow the complement cascade.

topics.label: C3 activation and its initiating pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how C3 becomes activated and accumulates on a target surface sufficiently to trigger complement effector activity.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement promotes the elimination of pathogens at an infection site.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how complement regulators restrain activation to protect the body's own cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Staphylococcus aureus complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains bacterial adaptations that evade complement and how the antibody-binding property of one such adaptation can be exploited.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: The closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the next lecture's subject.
